title: Format a script with your own AI
description: Use Claude, ChatGPT, or another LLM to prepare Quickque Markdown, then import it locally without giving Quickque an AI dependency.
body:
# Format a script with your own AI

Quickque does not need a built-in AI service to organise a script. If you already use Claude, ChatGPT, or another large language model, you can give it the reusable prompt below, add your script, and ask it to return Quickque Markdown. Save that response as a `.md` file and drop it into Quickque, or paste it into the editor's **Markdown** view.

The AI service is used only before import. Quickque parses the result locally with deterministic rules. Once the formatted script is in Quickque, reading, editing, storage, Voice Follow, and compatible voice features do not send the script back to that AI service.

## Before you begin

- Decide whether the script is safe to share with your chosen AI provider. Check that provider's privacy, retention, and training settings, especially for confidential, unreleased, client, audition, legal, or personal material.
- Keep an untouched copy of the original script. A language model can accidentally omit or alter words even when told not to.
- Use the full prompt below. It tells the model to format rather than rewrite.

## Reusable Quickque formatting prompt

Select **Copy** on this block, or [download the prompt as Markdown](/prompts/quickque-script-formatter.md) and attach it to your AI conversation.

```text
You are a formatting assistant. Convert the script I provide into Quickque Markdown without rewriting, summarising, correcting, embellishing, or censoring the words.

Return only the finished Quickque Markdown. Do not wrap it in a code fence. Do not add an introduction, explanation, checklist, or download link.

Quickque Markdown rules:

1. Put exactly one script title at the top as:
   # Script title
2. Divide a presentation into useful speaking sections. Start every section with:
   ## Section title
3. For a play, scene, self-tape, interview, or multi-speaker script, make each spoken turn its own section and put the speaker cue on a separate line:
   ## Short turn label
   **Character name:**
   Spoken words
4. Put stage directions, delivery notes, camera notes, and other unspoken instructions on their own lines beginning with:
   > Direction or note
5. Preserve every spoken word, spelling, punctuation mark, paragraph break, and intentional repetition from the source. Do not improve the writing unless I explicitly ask you to.
6. Do not invent dialogue, speakers, directions, section content, or missing facts.
7. Do not treat a name mentioned inside ordinary prose as a speaker cue.
8. If the source already has headings, use them as section titles where sensible. If it has no headings, add short neutral section titles based only on the text.
9. If a presentation is very long, split it at natural topic changes. Do not split individual sentences.
10. Use speaker names consistently. Keep the source spelling of each name.
11. Do not use Markdown formatting for emphasis, links, tables, images, or lists. Quickque only needs the title, section headings, speaker cues, directions, and plain spoken text.
12. If a spoken line literally begins with #, ##, >, or a speaker-shaped label such as **Name:**, prefix that literal line with a backslash so Quickque speaks it instead of treating it as structure.
13. Remove page numbers, repeated document headers, repeated document footers, and obvious copy-and-paste artefacts only when they are clearly not part of the script.
14. If something is ambiguous, preserve it as spoken text rather than guessing.

Before answering, silently check that:
- there is one # title and at least one ## section;
- no original spoken words were lost or changed;
- every speaker cue ends with a colon inside the bold markers;
- unspoken directions begin with >;
- the answer contains only Quickque Markdown.

SCRIPT TO FORMAT:

[Paste the complete script here]
```

## Steps

1. Open a new conversation in your chosen AI service. Paste the prompt, then replace `[Paste the complete script here]` with the complete script. For a long document, attach the original file if the service supports attachments and tell it that the attachment is the script to format.

2. Send the request. The response should begin with one `#` title, contain `##` section or turn headings, and contain no commentary outside the formatted script.

3. Compare the response with the original. Check names, figures, quotations, punch lines, legal wording, repeated phrases, and the beginning and end. Formatting is useful only if the spoken text remains accurate.

4. For a file workflow, paste the response into a plain-text editor and save it as a UTF-8 file ending in `.md`, such as `quarterly-update.md`. Do not save the surrounding AI chat or a screenshot.

5. In Quickque, select **Import document** or drop the `.md` file on the scripts workspace. Review the title and Markdown text, then choose **Save as Script**. The local parser creates sections, turns, characters, and notes from the markers.

6. Alternatively, create a script, open **Markdown** in the editor, paste the response, and select **Save script**. Invalid structure stays open with a line-specific error instead of replacing the saved script.

7. For a performance, open **Scene Partner** after import. Confirm the cast, mark your own roles as **In Person**, assign voices only where wanted, and rehearse a short section before relying on the full script.

## What the markers mean

- `# Title` names the script and must appear once at the top.
- `## Section` creates a presentation section or performance turn.
- `**Alex:**` assigns the following spoken text to Alex. New names create cast entries locally.
- `> Crosses to the window` creates an unspoken note or stage direction.
- Ordinary lines are spoken text. Quickque does not render or execute HTML from this format.

## Expected result

The imported Quickque script has a title and ordered sections rather than one unstructured block. Performance scripts also have consistent character turns and separate notes. The script remains available without an internet connection after import. Quickque does not call the AI provider, store an AI credential, or require the provider to read or perform the script.

## Troubleshooting

- **The AI rewrote the script:** start again with the untouched source and repeat that it must preserve every spoken word. Compare the complete result before import.
- **The answer includes an explanation or code fence:** ask for only raw Quickque Markdown, without opening or closing backticks. Remove those backticks before saving the file.
- **Quickque reports a line error:** check that the single `#` title is first, section headings use `##`, and speaker cues use the exact `**Name:**` form.
- **A direction is spoken aloud:** put it on its own line beginning with `>`.
- **A speaker becomes part of the dialogue:** make the cue a separate line and keep the colon inside the final bold markers, as in `**Alex:**`.
- **The import creates the wrong title:** edit **Script Title** during review, or correct the first `#` line.
- **The script is confidential:** do not submit it to an external AI service unless its terms and your permissions allow that use. Format it manually in Quickque instead.
- **The file will not import:** confirm it is plain UTF-8 text with a `.md` or `.markdown` extension, not a Word document renamed to Markdown.
